changes: Baladeva (p5): role changed from 'king' to 'other'. He reigned when the palm-leaf exemplar was copied in NS 180, not when this VS 1982 copy was made.
Notes corrected: 'nepālarājakīyapustakālayasthitaṃ' says the exemplar was kept in the Nepal Royal Library. It does not say the exemplar was copied there.
Purpose rewritten as a short English summary.
Added relation p2 servant_of p1 (prime minister under the king).
Hemarāja: the catalogue calls him 'Donor', but the colophon does not support this. He commissioned the copy for his own library, so he is kept as commissioner and owner, not donor.
Added the exemplar date and Candraśaṃśera's second spelling to the notes.

persons.name: Pūrṇaprasāda
persons.evidence: tadājñayā pūrṇaprasādaśarmaṇā likhitam idaṃ pustakaṃ ... pāṭhāntarair yāvac chakyaṃ saṃskṛtaṃ ca

purpose: for installation in Hemarāja's own library, the Bhāratībhavana
notes: This is a modern copy made in VS 1982 (c. 1925–26 CE). It was copied from an old palm-leaf exemplar kept in the Nepal Royal Library ('nepālarājakīyapustakālayasthitaṃ'). That exemplar is dated NS 180 Māgha śukla 3 (c. 1060 CE) in the reign of Baladeva, so Baladeva is the king of the exemplar, not of this copy. The scribe says he collated other old palm-leaf manuscripts and corrected the text from their variant readings. The colophon also praises events of that year and the year before: Candraśaṃśera abolished slavery, freeing about 51,000 slaves with compensation paid to their owners; he received British, Chinese and French honours; a new Anglo-Nepalese treaty was made; and the roof of Paśupatinātha was regilded. Candraśaṃśera is spelled 'candraśaṃśerevarmaṇo' at the second mention. The closing phrase 'ekatamena bhaktaparamānunedam alekhi' (garbled; it ends 'this was written') is presumably by the scribe Pūrṇaprasāda. The catalogue lists Hemarāja as 'Donor'. The colophon makes him commissioner and owner, not donor.
